Definitely worth Visiting!!!!!!

I tried their breakfast combo, which cost me ₹131 after applying GST.

My first impression was that it was such a small quantity that it wouldn't even fill the stomach of a single person. However, as soon as I started eating, I was pleasantly surprised.

1) The quality - It was the best I've had, and I didn't regret paying for it. It was really nice.

2) Taste - It had a homely taste. Yes, they do take time to serve you because everything is prepared freshly, but the taste is really nice. 3) Quantity - No matter how it looks on the plate, it's enough for an average healthy person. I was on an empty stomach when I had it, and it made me so full that I had my evening snack directly after breakfast.

4) Location - It's in the heart of Mumbai, near the railway station, and the location and ambiance are just too good.

5) Price range - Being in South Mumbai, in a prime location, what they are offering at this price is just awesome. Except for the buffet, other dishes on the menu are reasonably priced.

Conclusion: GO FOR IT. I am eager to go again. HIGHLY RECOMMENDED

Sri Krishna Restaurant is a place I’ve visited a few times over the years, and it continues to be a dependable option in the Mumbai dining scene, especially for South Indian vegetarian food.

One of the standout items here, in my experience, is the Dahi Vada, which I’ve had on multiple occasions and would definitely recommend. It’s consistently well-prepared and enjoyable.

On my most recent order, I also tried the Medu Vada and Rava Masala Dosa. While the food overall was good, I wasn’t particularly impressed with the sambar that accompanied the vada. Since sambar plays a key role in the dish, this did affect the overall experience for me. The rest of the preparation, however, was satisfactory.

They also offer a variety of ice creams, and the mango option we tried was quite good and made for a nice finish to the meal.

Service here is excellent. The staff are attentive and helpful, with waiters proactively suggesting dishes and offering recommendations in a thoughtful, non-pushy manner and something that enhances the overall dining experience.

featured_reviews.name: Amrutjyoti Shinde
featured_reviews.review_text: Heard a lot about this place from reels, and was not disappointed. Went with 3 friends around 3:30 pm on 14th Feb. It was not crowded at all. Then the Goli Bhaji and Mangalore Buns were absolutely delicious, not too sweet, perfectly balancing the sweetness with the coconut chutney. Then we got 4 different doses, and the Ghee Podi Benne Masala Dosa (jain) was the bestseller for a reason. First bite was heavenly and comforting, and the masala was made of raw banana, and was in sufficient quantity. The dosa was only so flavorful, there was no need of sambar or chutney. If you take regular dosa, you get an additional tomato garlic chutney. My friend ordered the Mulbagal Dosa, which they claim to have started the 1st time in Mumbai. Some might say you would get doses at cheaper prices elsewhere, but their price reflects their commitment to perfection and love towards serving people. I will definitely visit this place again..!!

featured_reviews.name: Prachiti Gadekar
featured_reviews.review_text:
If you’re craving an authentic Gujarati feast with a seasonal twist, Gujju Bhai No Thali is absolutely worth a visit right now!

The highlight of the experience is their unlimited aamras, served fresh as a summer special—and honestly, it steals the show. Sweet, rich, and perfectly chilled, it pairs beautifully with their hot, fluffy puris… pure comfort on a plate.

The thali itself is incredibly wholesome and satisfying. It starts off with refreshing drinks like chaas and pudina pani, setting the tone for what’s to come. The appetisers—kachori, dhokla, and chaat tart—are all fresh and flavourful, giving you that perfect mix of crunch, spice, and tang.

Moving to the mains, you’re treated to four different sabjis, two dals, and a classic Gujarati kadhi that strikes the perfect balance of sweet and tangy. Pair these with soft phulkas or puris, and it’s a complete meal in itself. You also get options like jeera rice and comforting dal khichdi, which just add to the homely feel of the meal.

And just when you think you’re done, the desserts keep coming! From warm halwa to the indulgent malai sandwich, everything feels like a celebration of flavours.

Overall, Gujju Bhai No Thali delivers a hearty, value-for-money dining experience with that signature Gujarati hospitality. With the mango season in full swing, the unlimited aamras makes it even more special—definitely not to be missed!
